item.title: Botanical Garden of the City of Neuchâtel
item.description: The Botanical Garden of the City of Neuchâtel contributes living collections, ethnobotanical expertise, and garden workflows to DBGI. Its team supports sampling, collection curation, and the connection between botanical knowledge and open scientific reuse.

item.title: Botanical Garden of the University of Fribourg
item.description: The Botanical Garden of the University of Fribourg contributes living-collection expertise, horticultural knowledge, and sampling workflows to DBGI. Its collections support the initiative’s work on plant chemodiversity and reusable botanical metadata.

item.title: Flore-Alpe Garden of Champex
item.description: Flore-Alpe contributes alpine botanical collections and mountain-plant expertise to DBGI. The garden supports sampling workflows that connect living collections with metabolomics and open biodiversity knowledge.

item.title: Prague Botanical Garden
item.description: Prague Botanical Garden collections are connected to DBGI through the Prague team working on plant specialized metabolites, mass spectrometry, and metabolomics. The garden contributes living-collection material to DBGI sampling and profiling workflows.

item.title: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew
item.description: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew contributes botanical collections, living-collection expertise, phytochemistry, and science-policy perspectives to DBGI. Kew’s participation strengthens the initiative’s connection between sampled collections, plant chemistry, and reusable open knowledge.
